proposals.motivation: Earlier evaluation of the Li3PO4 phosphate coating (mp-aaaaaegs) suggested that Li-rich oxyanion coatings are a viable direction. Li3BO3 tests a different anion chemistry in the same Li-rich oxyanion class.

proposals.hypothesis: Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich zirconate with fully oxidized Zr4+ and O2- anions. Zr4+ is very hard to reduce, so the sulfide electrolyte should not attack it, and the oxide should be a wide-gap electronic insulator. Its high Li content should limit Li-depletion-driven interdiffusion with LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, following the Li-rich oxide idea behind the Li8ZrO6 proposal.
proposals.motivation: Earlier Li8ZrO6 proposal (Li-rich oxide with a non-reducible d0 cation) suggested that Li-rich Zr oxides are a promising coating direction. Li6Zr2O7 keeps that chemistry at a lower Li:Zr ratio, which is available in the candidate list.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, Li-conducting, electrochemically robust phosphate. It is a well-known protective coating for cathodes in sulfide-based solid-state batteries, and its oxide-rich composition should limit reactive interdiffusion with both LiCoO2 and Li6PS5Cl at 4.0 V.

Li3BO3 is a Li-rich, wide-gap oxyborate that should be electrochemically stable at 4.0 V and electronically insulating. Its oxide anion framework and high Li content should limit reactive interdiffusion with LiCoO2 and with the sulfide electrolyte, similar to the protective role of the Li3PO4 coating. It belongs to a borate family not yet tested.
proposal.motivation: Earlier evaluation of the Li3PO4 phosphate coating (mp-aaaaaegs) suggested that Li-rich oxyanion coatings are a viable direction. Li3BO3 tests a different anion chemistry in the same Li-rich oxyanion class.

proposal.hypothesis: Li4P2O7 is a Li-rich pyrophosphate with a wide band gap and a fully oxidized P(V) framework, closely related to the Li3PO4 coating already tested. Its high Li content and oxyanion chemistry should limit reactive interdiffusion with LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte at 4.0 V while staying electronically insulating.
proposal.motivation: Earlier evaluation of the Li3PO4 phosphate coating (mp-aaaaaegs) suggested Li-rich oxyanion coatings are a viable direction. Li4P2O7 stays in that phosphate chemistry but changes the P-O connectivity and Li:P ratio, so it is a close refinement.

proposal.hypothesis: Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich aluminosilicate built from fully oxidized Al3+ and Si4+ and oxide anions. It should be a wide-gap insulator, and its high Li content and oxyanion framework should limit reactive interdiffusion with LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte at 4.0 V. Unlike Ti4+-containing oxides, it has no easily reduced cation that the sulfide could attack.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 coating (mp-aaaaaegs) showed that Li-rich oxyanion coatings are a viable direction. Li5Al(SiO4)2 tests a silicate chemistry not yet explored, with a higher Li content than most silicates in the list.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3Al(BO3)2 is a Li-rich oxyborate built from fully oxidized Al3+ and B3+ with oxide anions. It should be a wide-gap electronic insulator, and its high Li content and non-reducible cations should limit reactive interdiffusion with LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte at 4.0 V. It tests a borate chemistry in the same Li-rich oxyanion class as the Li3PO4 result.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 evaluation (mp-aaaaaegs) suggested Li-rich oxyanion coatings are a viable direction. Li3Al(BO3)2 carries that idea into a borate family not yet tested among the evaluated candidates.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, fully ionic Li-rich halide with a highly oxidized, non-reducible F- anion. It should be a strong electronic insulator and electrochemically stable at 4.0 V vs Li. Its fluoride chemistry is thermodynamically compatible with both LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte, and LiF is a common protective coating in sulfide cathode work. It is also a different family from the earlier oxyanion (phosphate, borate, silicate) choices.

Li2O is a wide-gap, fully ionic, Li-rich oxide with a non-reducible O2- anion and no transition-metal or easily reduced cation. Its high Li content and oxide chemistry should limit reactive interdiffusion with LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte at 4.0 V while remaining electronically insulating. It tests a simple oxide family not yet covered by the phosphate, borate, silicate, and fluoride choices.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 choice (mp-aaaaaegs) suggested Li-rich oxide coatings are a viable direction, and Li2O extends that idea to a simpler oxide chemistry.

proposal.hypothesis: Li8ZrO6 is a very Li-rich oxide with fully oxidized Zr4+ and O2- anions. Zr4+ is hard to reduce, so the sulfide electrolyte is unlikely to attack it, and the oxide framework should stay electronically insulating with a wide gap. Its high Li content should limit Li-depletion-driven interdiffusion with LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, similar to the protective Li-rich oxyanion idea.

Li8SiO6 is a very Li-rich orthosilicate with fully oxidized Si4+ and O2- anions. Si4+ is very hard to reduce, so the sulfide electrolyte should not attack it, and the oxide framework should be a wide-gap electronic insulator. Its high Li content should limit Li-depletion-driven interdiffusion with LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, following the Li-rich oxide idea behind the Li8ZrO6 proposal.
proposal.motivation: Earlier proposal of Li8ZrO6 (Li-rich oxide with a non-reducible d0 cation) suggested that very Li-rich oxides are a promising coating direction. Li8SiO6 keeps that Li-rich oxide chemistry but swaps in Si4+, which is smaller and even more resistant to reduction.
